capacity_basis.peak_assumption: At most 70 requests in 60 seconds; at least 88% request-rate headroom against the estimate
capacity_basis.headroom: At most 70 requests in 60 seconds; at least 88% request-rate headroom against the estimate
capacity_basis.failure_budget: zero uncounted protected effects when the store is unavailable or uncertain
workload_assumptions: One developer, one process, local data, no hosted traffic; present only under COBUDGET_IDENTITY_PROVIDER=local and refused at startup otherwise (design section 5.3); every read decrypts the live outbox rows of the simulated adapter (FIDELITY_LABEL simulated)

safe_counting_key.rotation_behavior: dual-read/single-write for at least 120000 ms; carry forward the greater count
safe_counting_key.privacy_basis: No subject locator, presented code, ceremony id or destination is used before authentication; the loopback transport cohort is the only counted dimension (AL-266-001).

anti_lockout_rule.pool_isolation: `proto-invitation-ceremony-v1` (new set; CBD266-INVITATION-RECORDS-001, the `proto-identity-ceremony-v1` values on `surf-266-invitation-accept`): the pre-authentication invitation ceremony routes (resolve, verify-channel, decline) count by network cohort plus exact surface only; no presented code, ceremony id, destination or claimed subject is a counting dimension, so an attacker cannot exhaust a victim pool by naming it (AL-266-001). `attackable_dimensions: [privacy_network_cohort_v1]`; `victim_bound_dimensions: []`; `independent_recovery_surface_id: null`. A verify-channel or decline request that names no resolvable ceremony is denied before any counter is touched (SEC-STAGES-F02 precedent), so a flood of unresolvable requests cannot exhaust the pool a real in-flight ceremony needs. The authenticated half of the ceremony (attach, disclosure read, accept) counts on the actor's own mutation and read pools (OQ-IV-003), never here. `exhaustion_state_effect: none`; reset authority is `local prototype operator / restore counter service only`; notification is uniform and content-safe; verify `FX-266-PUBLIC-COHORT-ISOLATION` and `VT-94-065`.
anti_lockout_rule.reset_authority: local prototype operator / restore counter service only
anti_lockout_rule.notification_behavior: uniform and content-safe; reveals neither existence nor remaining quota

capacity_basis.sustained_capacity: 2 ceremony requests/second in one local process; not measured - Implementation estimate dated 2026-09-15. Each resolve costs one HKDF derivation plus one HMAC per real invitation code row in the deployment (the run-to-completion constant-time scan of SEC-PK5-R02 as widened by R-02 / PK5FIX-F03), so the per-request CPU cost grows with the number of real code rows ever dispatched; the 15-per-minute-per-cohort ceiling is what bounds that unmetered cost until the code_selector column lands
capacity_basis.peak_assumption: At most 15 ceremony requests in 60 seconds per cohort; at least 87% request-rate headroom against the estimate at prototype code-row counts (tens of rows)
capacity_basis.headroom: At most 15 ceremony requests in 60 seconds per cohort; at least 87% request-rate headroom against the estimate at prototype code-row counts (tens of rows)
capacity_basis.failure_budget: zero uncounted protected effects when the store is unavailable or uncertain
workload_assumptions: One developer, one process, loopback traffic, simulated local delivery adapter, no email provider, no hosted traffic
Resolve is O(every real code row) HKDF+HMAC per request (SEC-PK5-R02, PK5FIX-F03); revisit the record when the code_selector column lands or before any hosted environment
